portfolio_view: Four picks span four distinct sectors — private banking (Federal Bank), specialty chemicals/CDMO (Navin Fluorine), shipping (Great Eastern Shipping), and textiles (KPR Mill) — deliberately avoiding the Financial Services concentration in the broader candidate pool. Two (Federal Bank, Navin Fluorine) are high-quality but already priced near highs, and one (GESHIP) rides an active, reversible geopolitical event, so in this DEFENSIVE regime (35.6% of universe above 200-DMA) these should be treated as half-size, selective entries, not full-conviction bets. We pass on daily-analyst BUYs CUPID and ORIENTHOT (no clean tradeable plan / lacks a verifiable second-order driver versus our picks) and SHYAMMETL and SOUTHBANK (solid, but duplicate sector exposure already covered by stronger names here).
theme_read: Shipbuilding & marine is the hottest theme on the map (96/100) and is now reinforced by a genuinely new driver — the West Asia crude/war shock — extending it beyond pure shipbuilders (KMEW, GPPL) into tanker owners like GESHIP; price (3m +5.1%) hasn't caught up to the news, but the driver itself is already cooling (Saudi-Iran talks Oct 26 pulled Brent back from $120), so mechanical heat here may be trailing a fading catalyst rather than leading a growing one. Textiles & apparel PLI (heat 67.3, "strengthening") is a case of heat running ahead of the real story at the name level — KPRMILL is tagged a beneficiary of PLI Round 4, but that scheme targets MMF/technical textiles, not KPR's cotton-knit base, and the score doesn't capture the real headwind of 26-27% US tariffs already cutting Indian apparel exports. Specialty chemicals & China+1 (66.7) checks out best at the name level — NAVINFLUOR's growth is validated against a dated, real driver (China's Oct 16 export-control expansion) — and is still early on price (3m -7.9%) even though the stock itself is fully valued. EMS (heat 33, lowest, now an explicit strengthening headwind from the DRAM/NAND cost shock) is rightly avoided — SYRMA was on the candidate list and not selected. Federal Bank's strength sits outside this theme map entirely — an idiosyncratic asset-quality story, not a thematic one.

Governance is excellent: 18 consecutive dividends, a ₹900cr buyback with promoters explicitly excluded.

picks.watch_for: any Houthi or Saudi-Iran de-escalation headline — this is a geopolitical trade, not a structural one.

picks.watch_for: further erosion in US apparel export volumes or continued promoter stake decline.
